cryptohome: Retry chall-resp decrypt errors Add retry logic into the decryption operations of challenge-response mounts (a.k.a. smart card login). This allows to overcome transient TPM errors, for example the errors caused by hitting the maximum number of simultaneously allowed TPM 2.0 sessions (which is currently 3) due to some parallel background activity in the OS. In particular, such problematic scenarios occur quite often during automated testing: during handling the CheckKeyEx request that is made shortly after a MountEx request, in which case our CheckKeyEx handler is fighting with the PKCS11 token initialization logic in the chaps daemon. BUG=chromium:842791,chromium:985509 TEST=(a) tast run $IP hwsec.ChallengeResponseMount; (b) issue CheckKeyEx command for a challenge-response mount quickly after the MountEx command Change-Id: Ic9797caa76713aa9d9d8b02591d0f65f47f10dd5 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1709317 Tested-by: Maksim Ivanov <emaxx@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Maksim Ivanov <emaxx@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Andrey Pronin <apronin@chromium.org>

update_kernel: Iterate over all kernel releases for depmod This code intends to run depmod on all the different versions of kernel modules in /lib/modules/ on the DUT. If there's more than one release in that directory we'll end up in a situation where the REMOTE_OUT variable contains space separated kernel versions and then the depmod command won't be run. Let's create an array out of the REMOTE_OUT variable and then iterate over the elements in the array instead so that we always run depmod on all kernel releases. BUG=None TEST=Run update_kernel on a DUT with many directories in /lib/modules and see the loop run many times in this script with the proper directory each time Change-Id: I9a7b3c534f9669950fb1c9362bfb31cfa2d8855c Signed-off-by: Stephen Boyd <swboyd@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1724860 Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Jack Rosenthal <jrosenth@chromium.org>

Fix definition of ESYSROOT to use SYSROOT's prefix For a given location, we were basing ESYSROOT on the prefix of that location instead of the prefix used by the SYSROOT location. For example, if BROOT=/foo, ROOT=/bar, EPREFIX=/baz, EROOT=/bar/baz, and SYSROOT=/ then ESYSROOT should be /foo, not /baz. vm_tools: sommelier: Fix wayland data transfers Wayland data transfers using wl_data_offer::receive and wl_data_source::send only ever worked by chance. The transfer code would delete the read event source when it ran out of data with the intention that the writer would finish writing and then clean up, but the writer could not be enabled for events at that time, so it would never wake up and the transfer would appear to fail. The specific application response to this varied, which made uncovering this issue more difficult. Some versions of GTK3 close their end of the pipe before sommelier does, this would cause sommelier to get a WL_EVENT_ERROR on the write source, prompting it to end the transfer. Others would ignore the uncompleted transfer, prompting bug reports of wayland pasting not working correctly. wl-clipboard would print out all data as it arrived which, combined with the gtk3 bug concealing this one, appeared to be a bug in wl-clipboard. TEST=manually tested BUG=chromium:986835 Change-Id: I788bfc4d9b1e13221ad8b56e826e550184c3a93e Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1722645 Tested-by: Fergus Dall <sidereal@google.com> Commit-Ready: Fergus Dall <sidereal@google.com> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Nic Hollingum <hollingum@google.com> Reviewed-by: David Reveman <reveman@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Stephen Barber <smbarber@chromium.org>

cryptohome: Skip useless migrations of chall-resp keysets Avoid trying to migrate the challenge-response keys when it's unnecessary (currently - always). The old code was seeing two facts - the TPM is available and that the keyset is not encrypted via the TPM - and therefore was trying to perform the migration (re-encryption) of the keyset. This was anyway producing the same keyset, so this all was just a waste of resources. If any of the patches fail to apply, then the script will print to stdout all patches that have applied successfully up to the failed patch and then 'die' will be called.
